- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Griot music influences contemporary West African styles like Afrobeat and Highlife.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mbube music has impacted Western music styles like Doo-wop and Gospel.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Taarab music has influenced contemporary genres in East Africa, such as Bongo Flava and Nairobian music.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Juju music has influenced contemporary Nigerian popular music genres like Afrobeat and Fuji.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Congolese rumba music has influenced salsa and other Latin dance styles.
- [USER] User expressed surprise at the influence of traditional African music on contemporary genres.
- [USER] User requested more information on how Congolese rumba music has impacted Latin American music.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Congolese rumba music significantly impacted Latin American music in the 1960s and 70s.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Congolese musicians like Tabu Ley Rochereau and Franco Luambo Makiadi gained fame with their fusion of African rhythms and Latin American music, called "soukous."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Soukous rhythms influenced Caribbean styles like zouk and compas, and salsa music, particularly the "salsa dura" style.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Some Latin American artists, such as Celia Cruz, recorded songs with Congolese musicians.
